description: Arrange the steps to build a working Genie Space in the correct order.
instructions: A Genie Space is configured by selecting trusted assets, providing instructions, and tuning with feedback. Pattern: catalog → metric layer → trust → context → instructions → validate.

blocks.code: Pick the Gold tables and views that contain answers to business questions (orders, customers, products)
blocks.label: Select Source Tables

blocks.code: Create metric views for standard business metrics (net_revenue, customer_ltv, churn_rate)
blocks.label: Build Metric Views

blocks.code: In the Genie Space settings, mark the chosen tables/views/functions as Trusted Assets
blocks.label: Configure Trusted Assets

blocks.code: Add custom SQL/Python functions Genie can call to compute on the fly (e.g., cohort_retention)
blocks.label: Add Trusted Functions

blocks.code: Write plain-English Genie Instructions: 'When users say revenue, use net_revenue. Active user means logged-in within 30 days.'
blocks.label: Write Genie Instructions

blocks.code: Run sample questions, check the generated SQL, upvote good answers, edit and save fixes for bad ones
blocks.label: Test & Tune with Feedback

hints: Start with the source: Genie needs actual data to query
Metric views are how you teach Genie what 'revenue' or 'churn' means in your business
Trusted Assets is the governance layer — without it Genie can't see the table even if it exists
Functions let Genie compute things that aren't pre-aggregated (cohorts, forecasts)
Instructions disambiguate terms like 'revenue', 'active', 'churn' that mean different things in different companies
Feedback is the tuning loop — every edited SQL improves future answers
learnings: Trusted Assets are the security boundary for Genie
Metric Views are the semantic layer Genie reads first
Instructions handle ambiguity that schema metadata can't
Feedback creates a virtuous improvement cycle
